title: Chamier: faith is in the will — to believe in God is to love God
source_text: XXXVIII. Quibus plane similia leguntur apud Chamierum, qui etiam eodem argumento utitur, ut probet fidem esse in voluntate, & non solum in intellectu. Omnis amor, inquit, est actus voluntatis; at fides est amor; ergo est actus voluntatis. Fidem autem esse amorem, probat quia vera fides est ea quae credit in Deum: At credere in Deum est amare Deum, juxta illud Augustini, Quid est credere in Deum? credendo amare. Panstratiae tomo 3. lib. 12. cap. 4. numero 16.
pass_a_gloss: Things plainly similar are read in Chamier, who also uses the same argument to prove that faith is in the will, and not only in the intellect. Every love, he says, is an act of the will; but faith is love; therefore it is an act of the will. But that faith is love he proves because true faith is that which believes in God: But to believe in God is to love God, according to that of Augustine, What is it to believe in God? by believing to love. Panstratia volume 3, book 12, chapter 4, number 16.
pass_b_english: Chamier: same argument — faith in the will, not intellect alone.
Every love is a will-act; faith is love; therefore faith is a will-act.
True faith believes in God = loves God (Augustine).
